summary: White takes the ko first at B19, and Black needs only one approach, at A14 or F19. Once one of them is filled, Black's capture at A17 in the second ko already threatens to connect at A18 and win, so each side needs one capture and one more move. That is the switching ko you called a normal ko in 10403, so the leaf is S[A-1KO-]: Black needs two threats more than White, the same count as your A-2KO+. White's extensions at A14 and F19 are worth two more threats; they are left out here, as on leaves 2, 3, 7 and 8. The checker's A-2KO- counts the capture at A17 as a second approach and gets a count of 3, so it is wrong too. Separately, White's A16 at move 8 is a mistake: White's A19 there leaves Black no kill (seki). Add that refutation to the tree, or C19 at move 7 will rank equal to A19 once leaves 3 and 6 both read A-1KO-.

Each side's resource is worth one threat, which makes the full count 4. 8) Off the leaf's line, from the start: B18 A18 C18 D19 A17 B17 C19 A19 (White's A19 instead of A16 at move 8). Black fails even six threats ahead, and the class is SEKI.

checker_part: Approach count and, through it, the count and the KO sign. The profile's n_S=2 counts A17 as an approach, but A17 is Black's capture in the second ko: its outright line is A17, F19, A18, and the warning 'round 2: no free retake after the approach' is that capture, after which White is banned at A18 and must spend a threat. By the owner's 10403 answer (a switching ko read through a second ko is A-1KO-, not A-2KO+), that capture is no approach. So n_S=1, and v with one forced pass is 1 (barred), giving A-1KO- with label count 2. That equals the leaf's decided count with White's edge moves barred. D4's second-ko test did not fire, because F19 and A14 also keep v in round 1 and D4 tests only the first approach: the same gap as 10403. With n_S=2, the checker's KO- part (v=1) also absorbs one of White's edge resources; v is 0 with them barred, which would give the tree's A-2KO+. So the printed label count 3 is neither the structural count (2) nor the full count (4). The full count's extra 2 are White's edge resources, one on each side (A14 extension with B14/A13; F18/G19 against F19), not 1 unlocated.
earlier_research: This agrees with the second round's verdicts on leaves 3 and 7 (k103, k102: A-1KO-, count 2, with White's B14/A13 and F18/G19 edge resources left out of the label and a full count of 4). This leaf has the same count and the same two edge resources, so neither verdict is contradicted. Consequence for grading: with leaves 3 and 6 both A-1KO-, Black's A19 and C19 at move 7 would rank equal. But the tree's White A16 at move 8 is a mistake: White's A19 there leaves Black no kill (narrow area: Black fails even six threats ahead, class SEKI). The tree needs that refutation before leaf 6 is relabeled, or C19 will look as good as A19.
